metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that are consistent with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic exclusively on 'conflict trials' - trials where TTB and Tallying make deterministic but strictly opposite predictions. By focusing only on these trials, the metric directly isolates the divergence in the underlying decision rules. Under TTB, this metric will be close to 1 (modulo response noise), whereas under Tallying it will be close to 0, providing maximal discrimination between the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic's deterministic predictions on trials where it has a strict preference (i.e., one option has more winning features than the other). By design, the experiment includes many critical trials where Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) strongly disagree because the highest validity cue points to one option, while a larger number of lower validity cues point to the other. On these trials, Tallying will consistently choose the option with more winning cues, yielding a high score on this metric. In contrast, TTB will choose the option favored by the first cue, thereby systematically choosing against Tallying's prediction and yielding a much lower score (close to 0.25, as TTB only agrees with Tallying on a single trial type).

The experimental design pits WADD and Tallying against each other on every single trial. Specifically, the option that WADD prefers (due to high-validity features) is always the option that Tallying rejects (due to having fewer winning features). By computing the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the deterministic WADD prediction, we obtain a metric that will be very high (near 1.0) for subjects using WADD and very low (near 0.0) for subjects using Tallying.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with Tallying rather than the Weighted Additive Model (WADD) on three critical trial types. On these trials, Tallying favors the option with more winning features regardless of validity, whereas WADD favors the option with fewer but highly valid features. The metric will yield a high value (close to 1) for Tallying-simulated data and a low value (close to 0) for WADD-simulated data, providing strong discrimination.
